title: ddRADSeq
scope: Illumina ddRADSeq drawing and catalogue text, with a separately labeled primary-paper resolution. The d_ route preserves the depicted sequential digests; the p_ route records Peterson et al.'s simultaneous double digest. They are evidence views of the same ddRAD/ddRADSeq assay, not two validated interchangeable variants or parallel reactions on one sample. Genomic DNA fragments carry restriction-adjacent sequence for SNP discovery and genotyping. MiddRAD is included only to delimit the explicitly named related variant at the available abstract evidence level. Other related applications and RAD-family names are not assigned the depicted workflow.

states.label: Genomic DNA bearing restriction sites
features: Biological target and chemical substrate are genomic DNA; this is a DNA marker assay.
Left image labels Genome and Restriction sites. Blue genome tracks contain site marks; the yellow highlight has no stated legend and is not assigned a specific sequence or modification.
The two adjacent genome depictions are explanatory views of input DNA, not an evidenced transfer, separate specimen, or compartment.

The lower-left caption reads Double digest restriction-site associated DNA marker generation (ddRADseq). No restriction enzyme identities or molecular end-group chemistries are labeled in this drawing.

states.label: Genomic fragments from a simultaneous two-enzyme digest
features: Two restriction enzymes act together on genomic DNA; random shearing is replaced by sequence-specific fragmentation.
The final library targets fragments with one end generated by each enzyme; the digest mixture is not itself claimed to contain only this desired class.
EcoRI/MspI is one experimental pair reported in this paper, not a diagram label or a requirement for all ddRAD implementations.

states.label: Size-selected pool of adapter-ligated genomic fragments
features: The intended sequenced subset has one end generated by each restriction enzyme and falls within the selected size range.
Nearby or distant restriction-site pairs outside the size regime are excluded from the intended representation.
Representation favors fragments closest to the size-selection target; loci do not have guaranteed uniform coverage across samples.

evidence.locator: Methods, Double Digest Restriction Associated DNA (ddRAD) Sequencing, [b00013]
evidence.quote: produces sequencing libraries consisting of only the subset of genomic restriction digest fragments generated by cuts with both REs (i.e., have one end from each cut) and which fall within the size-selection window (Figure 2B).

evidence.locator: Figure 2B caption, [b00008]
evidence.quote: Double digest RAD sequencing (ddRADseq), by contrast, uses a two enzyme double digest followed by precise size selection that excludes regions flanked by either [a] very close or [b] very distant RE recognition sites, recovering a library consisting of only fragments close to the target size (red segments).

evidence.locator: Methods, Double Digest Restriction Associated DNA (ddRAD) Sequencing, [b00014]
evidence.quote: shared bias in region representation favoring fragments closest to the mean of size selection, in turn, biases independent samples (e.g., from different individuals) towards recovering the same genomic regions (Figure 2B).

states.label: Amplified ddRAD library carrying sample barcode and PCR index
features: The readout carrier is amplified genomic DNA insert sequence joined to sequencing adapters; no RNA or probe-derived surrogate is involved.
In the combinatorial implementation, the inline adapter barcode identifies a sample within a pool, and an index introduced by PCR distinguishes that pool from other pools reusing inline barcodes.
The inline barcode occurs at the first bases of a sequencing read; the PCR index is read in a separate Illumina multiplexing read.
Restriction-adjacent reads permit SNP discovery and genotype inference for represented loci, including reference-free analysis; this does not determine variants in unsampled genome intervals.
The described adapters and primers provide standard Illumina cluster-generation and sequencing-primer interfaces.
The paper also permits single-read or paired-end sequencing and inline-barcode-only identification without the multiplexing read; the graph shows its combinatorial indexing implementation.
Sequencing is the supported downstream interface, not an additional operation depicted in the Illumina image.
